title: Stats stream P-row schema grows an 18th field but the version marker stays 'v1'
evidence:
write_str(sb, "# pp stats stream v1 - deterministic per-tick stats (story 5.7; same seed + commands -> identical bytes)
")
+	write_str(sb, "# P <tick>,<pipe>,<tier>,<cap_units>,<offered>,<carried>,<dropped>,<util_pct>,<wE>,<wS>,<wB>,<cE>,<cS>,<cB>,<qE>,<qS>,<qB>,<tx_octets>  (util = HONEST windowed % — served work / (rate x window); tx_octets = window transmitted octets)
")
+		fmt.sbprintf(sb, "P,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d
",
detail: P rows append tx_octets (17→18 fields) yet the stream still self-identifies as v1; any v1-keyed consumer parsing 17 fields silently misparses or truncates every P row.
recommended_fix: Bump the stats-stream version marker (e.g. v2) or document the appended-column contract so consumers can detect the schema change.

title: CSV literal test pins tx_octets to 0 alongside old-semantics util=100 — an impossible pair
detail: Fixture keeps the backlog-era util=100 but appends tx_octets=0; honest 100% implies 45,000 octets (240×15×12.5). A regression always emitting 0 passes this pin.
recommended_fix: Re-derive the hand-built row under honest semantics with a non-zero, recognizable tx_octets value so a swap or constant-0 regression fails loudly.

title: Zero-capacity link would display ~800M rate; old cap_units>0 guard dropped
detail: transit_ticks maps capacity 0 to 1, so line_rate_bps yields ~800 Mbps for a dead link; the cap_units>0 guard was removed and queue rows draw rates unconditionally, so a zero-cap row reads '800M'.
recommended_fix: Return 0 from line_rate_bps (or skip the rate label) for zero capacity; reinstate a cap>0 check before displaying a pipe rate.

title: Chip widened 96→112 px, but main.odin and units.odin comments still cite a 96 px budget
evidence:
-TRAY_CHIP_W :: 96
+TRAY_CHIP_W :: 112
+		// Compact form fits the 96 px chip; the NOC rail carries the full "100 Mbps" label.
+// format_rate_compact — the tray-chip variant (the 96 px chip budget):
detail: One hunk widens the chip to 112 px; the shipped comments justifying the compact format's width still say 96 px — one place updated, dependents missed.
recommended_fix: Update both comments to the 112 px chip / 86 px text zone so the width rationale matches the constant.

title: node_health comment (and spec) quote 'util 150% …' but the format string drops the 'util' prefix
evidence:
+	// pipes). "util 150% (load 1.5 KiB / 33 Mbps)" — a 🔴 node stays
-	trace := fmt.tprintf("util %d%% (load %d / %d u)", pct, units, throughput)
+	trace := fmt.tprintf("%d%% (load %s / %s)", pct, pp.format_bytes(load_bytes), node_rate)
detail: The comment directly above the line quotes a string the line cannot produce — the 'util ' prefix was silently dropped from the trace text.
recommended_fix: Either restore 'util ' in the format string or correct the comment (and spec example) to the actual output.

title: NOC section headers hardcode 90/6/512 while predicates read the catalog values
detail: Thresholds are catalog-driven (pipe_red_pct, lane_queue_packets, pool_max_packets) plus a silent default param 90, yet the titles hardcode 90/6/512 — divergence makes labels lie.
recommended_fix: Format the catalog value into the section titles and remove the silent default parameter so measure and draw cannot disagree.

evidence:

+			// the honest utilization (canon-colored) + the line rate, right-
detail: The bar/count draws are inside a conditional block; the new text draws are after its closing brace. If that block is the visibility gate, clipped rows may draw at stale coordinates.
recommended_fix: Verify the gating; move the util/rate draws inside the same visibility check so off-panel rows render nothing.

title: Sub-1-Kbps branches of the rate formatters are untested; compact form emits a unitless number
detail: Below 1 Kbps, format_rate_compact returns a bare number ('30' beside '30K'/'100M' chips) and no units_test case pins this branch or format_rate's 'bps' branch.
recommended_fix: Add low-rate pins to test_units_formatters; consider a 'bps' suffix in the compact form to disambiguate from packet counts.

evidence:

+// in the ifHCOutOctets/ifSpeed pattern). Integer floor (standard: 187 of
